name: sg-louver
summary: Full-bleed hero running shader.gallery's louver: a low lamp washes a plaster wall while the shadow of venetian blinds stripes it on a slight diagonal, bottom bars knife-sharp and top bars melting into grey as each slat hangs farther from the wall.

colors.description: Four separate jobs rather than four poles: lamp core, wide wash and ambient, cool limb in the penumbra, hairline along each slat. Omit to read --fx-c1 through --fx-c4 off the section, which is what keeps the shader and the CSS resting state on one palette.

slatGap.description: Distance between successive shadow bars in CSS pixels, scaled to the display by the shader itself. Upstream default, range 16 to 160.

tiltRange.description: How far the slats swing over one breath, which is how wide the dark bars get at their widest. Upstream default, range 0 to 1.

penumbra.description: How fast the edge blur grows up the wall; 0 keeps every bar knife-sharp top to bottom. Upstream default, range 0 to 2.

driftSpeed.description: Lateral lamp drift, which shears the diagonal as it moves; 0 pins the light. Upstream default, range 0 to 1.2.

deviations.what: The four u_palette colours are ours, not upstream's `midnight` preset.
deviations.why: louver/meta.json names a palette as a string only; the table it resolves against lives in @shader-gallery/runtime, a package paw-fx does not vendor. Ours is a warm lamplight with a cool limb, chosen to match the CSS resting state, which reads the same --fx-c1..--fx-c4.

deviations.what: Rendered through paw-fx's own WebGL runtime (effects/_shared/glsl-mount.js) rather than @shader-gallery/runtime.
deviations.why: Seam. Upstream ships the .frag with no module around it. The GLSL itself is byte-identical to upstream and lives in shader.frag beside index.js.
